Subject: Region pinning questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning — that was helpful. We have a couple follow-up questions from our architecture and security teams around region pinning and handling PII:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that requests from our US region will be pinned to US-based compute and storage (including KV cache/backups)? What does region pinning look like for multi-tenant hosted customers?

2) In a failover scenario (regional outage), what are the cross-region failover semantics? Will requests be routed to EU/APAC and if so, do you have controls to prevent that for certain sensitive tenants?

3) How do backups and snapshots for model state and logs work? Are backups stored in the same region by default and can we opt into region-restricted backups?

4) For auditing, what logging controls are available (request logs, redaction of PII, retention windows)? Our security team wants to understand retention defaults and options to shorten retention for sensitive datasets.

I attached an internal requirements checklist (acme_pin_req.xlsx). Can you loop in your solutions/infra lead to provide technical detail?

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the clear list. Answering point-by-point below (high-level; happy to jump on a short technical session).

1) Region pinning (Hosted vs Dedicated/Private)
- Dedicated & Private: we can enforce strict region residency for both compute and persistent storage (KV caches, model caches, logs, backups). This is a contractual control — we deploy customer workloads into your chosen cloud region(s) and restrict routing and storage to those regions.
- Hosted (multi-tenant): we offer strong region affinity and static routing policies to keep traffic in-region where capacity permits. For strict regulatory requirements (e.g., financial PII that must not leave US), we recommend Dedicated/Private.

2) Cross-region failover behavior
- Default behavior: in a regional outage we will failover to the next available compatible region to preserve availability (this may route traffic to another region, e.g., US->EU).
- Opt-out / restricted mode: for customers who cannot tolerate cross-region failover, we offer a "no cross-region failover" option in Dedicated/Private which instead returns a configurable HTTP 503 until capacity in-region is restored or a manual override is applied.
- Failover activation: automated via health checks + routing policy. We can expose an SLA-informed failover window and keep failover actions logged for audit.

3) Backups and snapshots
- Backups are configurable per-deployment. Default for Dedicated/Private is same-region backups stored in customer’s region by default. For Hosted customers, backups are stored in the region of the serving cluster; we can provide single-region backups for certain enterprise tiers.
- Encryption & key management: backups are encrypted at rest. For Private, you can bring-your-own-keys (KMS/HSM). For Dedicated, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations.
- Retention & deletion: retention windows are configurable; we support ephemeral retention (e.g., 7/30/90 days) and can implement accelerated deletion policies for specific datasets on request.

4) Logging & PII controls
- Request logs: token-level request logs are available for debugging and billing. We provide tooling to redact PII at ingestion (regex-based & ML-assisted redaction) and also an option to disable persistent logging of request payloads for sensitive routes.
- Retention: default retention is 90 days for request logs in Hosted; Dedicated/Private can set retention to as low as 0 days for raw payloads (audit logs still retained per policy).
- Access & auditing: logs are audit-trailed with RBAC. We can provide periodic exports or set up push-based forwarding to your SIEM in-region.

Attachments I’m including: a short diagram for region pinning and backups (redwood-region-pinning-diagram.pdf) and a reference doc on logging controls (link in HubSpot).

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min technical call with our infra team tomorrow afternoon PST.
